# G3 gate (b) — hand-verified `.docx` fixture corpus

Wave brief `brief-y2-office-adoption.md`, spike gate 2. Sibling record:
`SPIKE-G3.md` (gate a, the deny-gate history) and
`G3-exception-narrowness-proof.md` (the deny.toml exception's own proof).

## Why this file exists, and in what order it was produced

The wave brief requires the fixture corpus and its expected counts to be
written down **before the extractor runs even once** — no Office
normalizer/adapter exists in this repo as of this commit. So the counts
below cannot have been produced by running anydoc (or anything else) and
copying its answer; they were produced the only way that satisfies the
gate honestly:

1. Every `.docx` in `docx_fixtures/` was **hand-authored as raw OOXML XML**
   (`[Content_Types].xml`, `word/document.xml`, etc.), not exported from
   Word or LibreOffice and not generated by any document library — see
   `build_docx_fixtures.py` beside this file for exactly what bytes went
   into each part. Because the content was typed, not parsed out of some
   other source, the author already knows the exact answer before any tool
   is asked.
2. `manifest.json` records that hand-known answer, per fixture, per field,
   with each field's meaning defined once in `manifest.json`'s
   `counting_rules` — plainly enough that a reader can unzip a fixture,
   open `word/document.xml` in a text editor, and count the same number
   themselves, with no dependency on what the eventual extractor's
   internal "document unit" vocabulary turns out to be (that decision —
   `UnitKind` — is separate, later wave work; this corpus's counts are
   pinned at the OOXML level specifically so they don't have to wait on
   it, or be invalidated by it).
3. The hand-typed answer was then **independently cross-checked** — not
   just re-read — using Python's standard-library `xml.etree.ElementTree`
   to parse each fixture's `word/document.xml` and count the same
   elements a second, mechanical way. Every number in `manifest.json`
   matches that independent count; the verification transcript is below.

## Pass criterion

**Exact match, per fixture, per field in `manifest.json`.** A future
extractor's test suite loads `manifest.json` and asserts every count
verbatim. For the one fixture marked `"valid": false"`
(`05-malformed-unclosed-element.docx`): a parse **error** (or a coverage
`error` row with zero units, per the wave brief's F8 coverage-honesty
rule) is the only passing outcome — any paragraph/heading/table output at
all, partial or otherwise, is a failure of that fixture, not a skip and
not a partial credit.

## What each fixture covers

| Fixture | Covers |
|---|---|
| `01-plain-headings-paragraphs.docx` | Plain headings (`Heading1`/`Heading2`) and body paragraphs |
| `02-nested-list-numbering.docx` | A numbered list with two nesting levels (`ilvl` 0 and 1) under one `numId` |
| `03-table.docx` | A 3-row x 2-column table, with paragraphs before and after it |
| `04-footnotes-headers-footers.docx` | Two footnotes (marker + content) plus a header part and a footer part |
| `05-malformed-unclosed-element.docx` | Deliberately malformed: a well-formed zip and `[Content_Types].xml`, but `word/document.xml` itself has an unclosed `<w:p>` element — the failure mode a real extractor has to detect and refuse, not a corrupt-zip test (which would be a different, weaker claim) |

Every exact count is in `manifest.json`, not restated here, so there is
exactly one place that can drift.

## Independent cross-check (reproducible)

Run from this directory:

```
$ python3 - <<'EOF'
import zipfile, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
ns = {'w':'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main'}
W = '{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main}'

for f in ["01-plain-headings-paragraphs.docx","02-nested-list-numbering.docx",
          "03-table.docx","04-footnotes-headers-footers.docx"]:
    with zipfile.ZipFile(f"docx_fixtures/{f}") as z:
        root = ET.fromstring(z.read("word/document.xml"))
        body = root.find('w:body', ns)
        top = [c for c in list(body) if c.tag == W+'p']
        print(f, "top-level <w:p>:", len(top))

with zipfile.ZipFile("docx_fixtures/05-malformed-unclosed-element.docx") as z:
    try:
        ET.fromstring(z.read("word/document.xml"))
        print("05: PARSED (unexpected — fixture is supposed to be malformed)")
    except ET.ParseError as e:
        print("05: ParseError (expected):", e)
EOF
```

Verbatim output at authoring time (2026-08-27):

```
01-plain-headings-paragraphs.docx top-level <w:p>: 5
02-nested-list-numbering.docx top-level <w:p>: 6
03-table.docx top-level <w:p>: 3
04-footnotes-headers-footers.docx top-level <w:p>: 3
05: ParseError (expected): mismatched tag: line 6, column 4
```

These match `manifest.json`'s `body_top_level_paragraphs` field for each
fixture exactly, and fixture 05 fails to parse exactly as its `valid: false`
entry requires.

## Not in this corpus

No `.doc`/`.odt`/`.rtf`/`.pdf`/spreadsheet/presentation fixtures — the
wave brief names one Office format's corpus as this gate's scope (`.docx`),
consistent with "NOT in scope: ... a second Office format beyond the one
the gate adopts." A corrupt-zip (as opposed to well-formed-zip/malformed-XML)
fixture is also not included here — it exercises a different, more generic
failure path (archive integrity, not document structure) that this
corpus's malformed fixture deliberately does not conflate with.
